gaps.title: Bank details captured as a file upload, but the decision defines structured account data
gaps.description: The captured New supplier form collects Bank details through a file chooser. DEC-001 states bank details are account name, sort code and account number. The mockup has no inputs for these three values, and it is unclear whether a supporting document upload is also wanted.
gaps.why_it_matters: The finance approver must confirm specific bank details by phone (DEC-004) and the payment system pays from them (DEC-003); both depend on account name, sort code and account number existing as data.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The registration form cannot be specified, and the verified and paid-to account details may not exist as checkable data.

gaps.title: Approval and verification steps not shown in the capture
gaps.description: Submit for approval has no target, and only the registration screen was captured. No screen, component or flow in the capture shows a finance approver reviewing a submitted supplier, recording the outcome of the phone verification, approving, rejecting, or the registrant receiving a rejected supplier to correct and resubmit. Supplier statuses (for example pending, rejected, approved) are not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-002 and REQ-003 are must-have requirements whose whole workflow (verify, approve, reject, resubmit) happens after submit, and none of it is in the capture.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The approval workflow, its statuses and the screens for approvers and registrants cannot be specified from the mockup.

gaps.title: Number of approvers and segregation of duties not decided
gaps.description: DEC-002 answered the rejection path but not how many finance approvers must approve a supplier, nor whether the person who registered a supplier (or who holds both roles) may also verify and approve it.
gaps.why_it_matters: Supplier approval releases the supplier for payment (DEC-003); one person registering, verifying and approving the same supplier is a classic payment-fraud path.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Role permissions and approval rules cannot be specified, and a single user could create and approve a payable supplier.
research_questions: What segregation-of-duties controls do common internal-control frameworks (for example COSO, or UK finance audit guidance) expect for vendor master data creation versus approval?
Do accounts-payable systems typically require one or two approvers for new supplier creation, and under what thresholds?

gaps.title: Changes to supplier and bank details after approval
gaps.description: Whether a registered or approved supplier can be edited, by whom, and whether a change to bank details returns the supplier to unapproved and requires re-verification is not decided. CQ-001 and CQ-004 asked this, but DEC-001 and DEC-004 did not answer it.
gaps.why_it_matters: If bank details on an approved supplier can change without re-verification, the 'verified before approval' rule can be bypassed after approval, and the payment system would pay an unverified account.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Payments could go to altered, unverified bank accounts (a common invoice/mandate fraud pattern).
research_questions: What controls do UK fraud-prevention bodies (for example UK Finance or Action Fraud guidance on mandate fraud) recommend when supplier bank details change?
Do accounts-payable systems usually revert a supplier to unapproved status when bank details are edited?

gaps.title: Record of the phone verification not defined
gaps.description: DEC-004 says a finance approver phones the supplier on a number from an independent source. What is recorded about this (who verified, when, which number and its source, the outcome) and whether it must be traceable later is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Verification is a manual off-system step that gates a payable approval; without a record, nobody can later show that the check happened or who did it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Approvals cannot be audited and disputed or fraudulent payments cannot be traced back to the verification decision.
research_questions: What audit evidence do auditors typically expect for call-back verification of supplier bank details?

gaps.title: Required fields, validation rules and error display
gaps.description: No required marker is visible on any field, and which fields are mandatory is not decided. DEC-001 says the VAT number is checked for format only, but not which country formats are accepted. Validation of sort code and account number, and the messages for validation errors, a blocked duplicate VAT number, or a submit failure, are not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[1], 'What is shown on validation errors...'

gaps.why_it_matters: Duplicate VAT numbers are blocked (DEC-001), so the registrant needs to know why a submission was refused; incorrect sort code or account number formats would reach the phone verification step.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Form rules and error behaviour cannot be specified; registrants may be blocked without explanation or submit malformed bank details.
research_questions: What are the format rules for UK VAT registration numbers (GB prefix, 9 or 12 digits, GBGD/GBHA forms), and should EU or other countries' formats be accepted?
What are the format rules for UK sort codes and account numbers, and is modulus checking (Vocalink/Pay.UK) commonly applied at entry?
How should form errors be presented to meet WCAG 2.2 AA (error identification, suggestion, status messages)?

gaps.title: Approved status hand-off to the payment system
gaps.description: DEC-003 says this feature only marks a supplier as approved so the payment system can pay it. How the payment system learns of the approval, and whether approval can be revoked or a supplier suspended afterwards, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The 'before it can be paid' rule is only enforced if the payment system reliably reads this feature's approval status, including any later withdrawal.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Unapproved or revoked suppliers could be paid, or approved suppliers could fail to become payable.

gaps.title: Who may register suppliers and who may see bank details
gaps.description: Whether roles other than procurement staff may register suppliers, and which roles may view bank details of submitted or approved suppliers, is not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[1], 'Who can submit a supplier for approval?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Bank account details are sensitive financial data and can identify sole traders; broad visibility increases fraud and data-protection exposure.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Permissions and data visibility cannot be specified, and bank details may be exposed to more users than necessary.
research_questions: Under UK GDPR, are bank details of sole-trader suppliers personal data, and what minimisation or access controls are expected?

gaps.title: Notifications for pending approval and rejection
gaps.description: Whether finance approvers are told a supplier awaits verification and approval, and whether the registrant is told of rejection (and why), is not stated. Whether a rejection reason is captured is not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[1], 'are the submitter or approver notified?'

gaps.why_it_matters: DEC-002 sends rejected suppliers back to the registrant to correct; without notice or a reason, the correction loop may stall and suppliers stay unpayable.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Submissions and rejections may sit unnoticed, delaying supplier onboarding.

gaps.title: Duplicate submissions and simultaneous approver actions
gaps.description: Behaviour when Submit for approval is pressed twice, when two registrants submit the same VAT number at once, or when two approvers act on the same supplier at the same time is not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-002, action 'Submit for approval' visibly_disabled false

gaps.why_it_matters: Duplicate VAT numbers are explicitly blocked (DEC-001); concurrent submissions could still create duplicates, and conflicting approve/reject actions could leave an ambiguous status.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Duplicate supplier records or contradictory approval outcomes.
research_questions: What patterns do business applications commonly use to prevent duplicate record creation from double submission and concurrent requests?

assumptions.text: Suppliers are UK-based with UK bank accounts, since DEC-001 refers to sort codes.
assumptions.why: Needed to scope VAT and bank-detail format research.
assumptions.impact: Validation research focuses on UK formats; foreign suppliers would need other formats (for example IBAN).
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether non-UK suppliers or non-UK bank accounts must be supported.

assumptions.text: The verifying finance approver and the approving finance approver may be the same person, as DEC-004 implies the approver performs verification.
assumptions.why: DEC-004 assigns the phone check to 'a finance approver' without saying it is the approving one.
assumptions.impact: Affects whether verification and approval are one step or two.
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether verification and approval are performed by the same person in one step.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Mockup captures Bank details as a file upload (SCR-002), while DEC-001 defines them as account name, sort code and account number (GAP-001).
Number of approvers and whether the registrant may approve are not decided (GAP-003).
Whether changed bank details must be re-verified is not decided (GAP-004).
